pillarForecast.why: Thrusters with a flame and real coasting are unmistakably a ship; this is the axis he raised, and the change is big enough to perceive (unlike grip 4).

Out-turning still works on paper (85px vs 130px), but only while thrusting toward the new heading; with coast drag 0.4 his dodges become committed slides, so the 'clever dodging' may turn into fighting the ship.
Still movement only, but rotate+throttle+brake puts attention on the controller, especially early; the 'I may miss this level of control' worry is likely to surface.
Flank spawns put pursuers on screen about half the run and the wave no longer eats them; he will notice chasers, though he may credit the fewer asteroids.
Side/ahead spawns at the screen edge plus inertia into death walls and moving wall gaps invite 'came out of nowhere' or 'couldn't stop in time' deaths.
The steady wave draws no complaint (fixes vanish silently); intensity now comes from on-screen pursuers, possibly tipping into 'too hard'.

biggestRisk: The thrusters' very low coast drag (speed falls only about a third per second) in narrowing lanes with death walls, moving wall gaps and faster on-screen pursuers: his favourite act, out-turning chasers, becomes a committed slide, deaths feel like the ship's fault, and he concludes he misses direct control ('go back to no momentum'), possibly while saying chasers on screen are much better.
abVerdict: He mostly won't name A vs B as a variant difference; his attention goes to thrusters and chasers. B (walls) is more likely to be mentioned by content ('walls of asteroids are cool / hard to thread with drift') and to kill him by rock; A runs go further. If he expresses a preference it leans B in sentiment (he already said a wall was fun) and A in results, with a real chance he asks for walls plus less drift.
